purpose: Second non-overlapping safety expansion focused on age, pregnancy/lactation, gastrointestinal, neurological, allergy, duration, and genotoxic-exposure constraints from official EMA/HMPC sources.
governance_note: This extension avoids the botanicals and claims used in Safety Extension 09 wherever possible and adds distinct high-risk safety assertions. No production safety rule is changed.

records.botanical_name: Senna alexandrina Mill. (Cassia senna L.; Cassia angustifolia Vahl)
records.safety_effect: Senna leaf medicines must not be taken during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

records.botanical_name: Senna alexandrina Mill. (Cassia senna L.; Cassia angustifolia Vahl)
records.population_or_drug: intestinal obstruction/stenosis/atony, appendicitis, inflammatory bowel disease, unexplained abdominal pain, severe dehydration
records.safety_effect: Senna leaf must not be taken in several obstructive, inflammatory, painful, or severely dehydrated gastrointestinal states.
Senna pod medicines must not be used in children under 12 years.

records.population_or_drug: patients using stimulant laxatives for longer than short-term treatment
records.safety_effect: Long-term use should be avoided because prolonged stimulant-laxative use may impair bowel function and lead to laxative dependence.

records.botanical_name: Frangula purshiana (DC.) A.Gray / Rhamnus purshiana DC.
records.safety_effect: Cascara medicines must not be taken during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

records.botanical_name: Frangula purshiana (DC.) A.Gray / Rhamnus purshiana DC.
records.safety_effect: Cascara should only be used in adults and adolescents over 12 years and must not be used in children under 12.

records.population_or_drug: achlorhydria, liver disease, gallstones, or other bile-related disorders
records.safety_effect: For minor gastrointestinal problems, peppermint oil must not be used in people with achlorhydria, liver disease, gallstones, or other bile-related disorders.
Peppermint oil preparations must not be used in children under 2 years old.

records.population_or_drug: children with a history of seizures
records.safety_effect: For cough/cold, muscle-pain and itching uses, peppermint oil medicines must not be used in children who have had seizures.

records.population_or_drug: patients allergic to caraway, Apiaceae family plants, mugwort, or birch
records.safety_effect: Caraway fruit medicines must not be used in patients hypersensitive to caraway, Apiaceae family plants, mugwort, or birch.

records.botanical_name: Foeniculum vulgare Mill. subsp. vulgare var. vulgare
records.population_or_drug: general population, pregnant/breastfeeding patients, and children under 12
records.locator: Final EU herbal monograph, section 6, p. 9/9
records.safety_effect: Because estragole is treated as a genotoxic carcinogen concern, exposure should be kept as low as practicably achievable, with explicit lower daily intake limits for pregnancy/breastfeeding and children under 12.
Reported adverse effects include severe allergic reactions with swelling of the face and difficulty breathing or swallowing.
